newsitem.title: USA: UK, Canada hopeful on Paris Club debt relief pact.
newsitem.headline: UK, Canada hopeful on Paris Club debt relief pact.

text.p: The finance ministers of Britain and Canada said on Saturday that they were hopeful of an early agreement on Paris Club debt relief of up to 80 percent for the world's poorest countries.
"I am optimistic," Canadian Finance Minister Paul Martin told reporters.
The issue is expected to be on the agenda of the Group of Seven finance ministers' meeting later in the day.
"I am hoping we might get agreement on 80 percent in the next few days," UK Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke said.
He and Martin were speaking at a news conference in Washington on demands by Commonwealth countries for faster progress in bailing impoverished debtor countries.
Martin declined to speculate whether G7 ministers would agree on the proposals at the meeting today.
Clarke said agreement on help for poor debtor nations was very close but warned against pushing for too much.
There has been pressure on the Paris Club of official creditors to boost the write-off to 90 percent from the current maximum of 67 percent.
Clarke said it was also important for the Paris Club not to put too bureaucratic a definition on what debt was eligible for help.
There have been arguments that under current rules, the Club could in the end forgive no more than 20 percent of the debt of the most deserving countries.
